skill.name: github-code-review
skill.description: Coordinates GitHub pull request code reviews with ruv-swarm agents, GitHub CLI workflows, quality gates, and review comments.
skill.summary: Run multi-agent GitHub pull request reviews with security, performance, architecture, and style checks.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: The audit confirmed a vulnerable webhook example that uses child_process.execSync with untrusted PR comment text. Most other static hits are Markdown code fences or expected GitHub CLI workflow examples. Documentation links and GitHub token login usage did not show exfiltration evidence.

remediation.issue: Unvalidated PR comment execution in webhook example
remediation.suggestion: Remove execSync or replace it with an allowlisted command dispatcher using argument arrays and verified webhook signatures.

remediation.issue: Webhook payload values interpolated into shell commands
remediation.suggestion: Validate PR numbers as integers and pass all values as arguments to spawn or execFile without a shell.

remediation.issue: Production workflow examples lack permission guidance
remediation.suggestion: Document least-privilege GitHub token scopes, signature verification, and reviewer approval before automated merge or approval.

static_findings.snippet: run: echo "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" | gh auth login --with-token
- ✅ Cache analysis results to avoid redundant work

finding_verdicts.reason: The webhook example imports child_process.execSync and uses it in the same handler. This enables shell execution in automation that processes GitHub webhook payloads.
The command interpolates event.pull_request.number from a webhook payload into execSync. It appears intended for GitHub automation, but the value is not validated before shell execution.
The command places event.comment.body into an execSync shell string. A crafted PR comment can inject shell syntax into the webhook host command.

content.user_title: Review GitHub Pull Requests with AI Agents
content.value_statement: Manual pull request review can miss security, performance, and architecture issues. This skill coordinates GitHub CLI workflows and ruv-swarm agents for structured review feedback.
actual_capabilities: Shows GitHub CLI commands for collecting pull request files, diffs, labels, and reviews.
Defines ruv-swarm review commands for security, performance, architecture, style, and accessibility checks.
Provides GitHub Actions workflow examples for automated pull request review and labeling.
Includes examples for generating inline review comments through the GitHub API.
Documents quality gates, review metrics, dashboards, and cross-PR analysis workflows.
Describes custom review agent configuration and registration.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI, repository access, and ruv-swarm commands to be available.
Command examples need validation before use in production automation.
The skill does not verify webhook signatures or permission scopes for users.
Review accuracy depends on configured agents and project context.

use_cases.title: Review Feature Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Coordinate security, performance, style, and architecture checks before a feature is merged.

use_cases.title: Screen Security-Sensitive Changes
use_cases.description: Focus review agents on authentication, authorization, secrets, and dependency risks in high-impact pull requests.

use_cases.title: Automate PR Quality Gates
use_cases.description: Build GitHub Actions workflows that collect PR context, run review agents, and post structured feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Basic PR Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one pull request
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pull request 123 with this skill. Focus on correctness, tests, and clear feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Security-Focused Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pull request 123 for security risks. Prioritize authentication, authorization, secrets, dependency issues, and unsafe input handling.

prompt_templates.title: Automated Workflow Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a repeatable CI review process
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitHub Actions workflow that runs multi-agent review on new pull requests and posts concise review comments.

prompt_templates.title: Custom Multi-Agent Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review planning for a large repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a multi-agent review plan for a large pull request. Include agent roles, quality gates, comment policy, and escalation rules.

output_examples.input: Review PR 123 for security and performance risks.
output_examples.output: A concise review summary with blocking security findings, performance notes, and suggested next actions.

output_examples.input: Prepare a GitHub Actions review workflow for pull requests.
output_examples.output: A workflow plan that gathers PR context, runs review agents, posts feedback, and applies review labels.

output_examples.input: Create a review plan for an authentication change.
output_examples.output: A focused plan with security agents, required checks, approval criteria, and audit trail expectations.

best_practices: Validate all PR comment commands before passing them to automation.
Use least-privilege GitHub tokens and document required permissions.
Keep review comments specific, actionable, and tied to changed files.
anti_patterns: Do not execute arbitrary PR comment text as a shell command.
Do not auto-approve or merge changes without clear human policy.
Do not post secrets, tokens, or private scan output in PR comments.

faq.question: What does this skill help review?
faq.answer: It helps review GitHub pull requests for security, performance, architecture, style, accessibility, and test concerns.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. Most examples use gh commands to read pull request data and post review feedback.

faq.question: Can it run inside GitHub Actions?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes workflow examples for automated review jobs and pull request labeling.

faq.question: Does it replace human review?
faq.answer: No. It supports reviewers with structured findings, but teams should keep human approval for important changes.

faq.question: What tools does it coordinate?
faq.answer: It coordinates GitHub CLI commands, ruv-swarm review commands, and Claude Code style agent workflows.

faq.question: What should users secure first?
faq.answer: Users should validate webhook payloads, restrict tokens, and avoid executing raw PR comments.
